title: Microsoft Purview DLP: start a Power Automate workflow when a rule matches (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the briefing understates potential licence costs and leaves documented Power Platform data-policy enforcement as an open question. The PowerShell parameter exists, but its reference does not explain how it configures the action; the UI reference also does not document the workflow action itself.

claims.where: Open questions; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Whether Power Platform data policies apply to flows using the Microsoft Purview connector remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Power Automate makers and users won't be able to start a flow that uses connectors that don't belong together or have been blocked by data policies. A background system process marks the flow as Suspended
claims.fix: Replace the applicability caveat and the Before rollout question with: 'Power Platform data policies govern connector combinations in Power Automate flows. A flow using connectors that are blocked or cannot be used together is suspended and cannot execute until the violation is resolved; runtime suspension is not instantaneous.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/dlp-impact-policies-apps-flows. Narrow the final Open question to: 'What does the Purview rule show when its linked Power Automate flow is suspended?'
